prompt: Some people think that schools should teach students according to their academic abilities, while others believe that it is better to have students with different abilities to study together. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
It is sometimes argued that schools should teach students in groups based on academic ability, whereas others believe that children of different levels should study together. I accept that ability grouping can be useful in some situations, but I believe that mixed-ability classes should remain the normal approach.

On the one hand, teaching students according to ability may make lessons more efficient. In a class of high achievers, teachers can move at a faster pace, introduce more demanding tasks and avoid spending too much time on basic explanations. Similarly, pupils who find academic work difficult may benefit from slower lessons, clearer explanations and more individual attention. If these groups are flexible rather than permanent, they can help different learners make progress at a pace that suits them.

However, I would argue that separating children too early can do more harm than good. Students placed in lower groups may feel that they have been labelled as weak, which could damage both their confidence and their ambition. By contrast, mixed classes allow learners to cooperate with classmates who have different strengths. A capable student who explains a problem to a friend, for example, often understands it more deeply, while the friend receives support in a relaxed and less intimidating way. It also prepares them for a society in which people rarely work only with those at the same level.

In my view, the best solution is to keep most classes mixed, while providing extra support for struggling learners and extension tasks for high achievers. This approach recognises academic differences without turning them into permanent labels.

In conclusion, although ability-based teaching has some advantages, mixed-ability education is generally better because it supports both academic progress and social development.
